steps.content: A blood moon fills your sight like the eye of the sky, gazing coldly down the earth.
You are standing in a sea of flowers, and the overflowing purple petals flood at you like a tidal wave.
Fear creeps up closer and closer. You can't help but run frantically.
But there is no escape. You are doomed to be devoured by the eye of the sky and the purple tide.
You open your mouth to call for help, but no words come out, nothing but your heavy panting noise.
In the flower fields around, eerie vines start to grow and entangle around your body. Chilling, mystical glimmers sprinkle on the purple petals in the moonlight.
You open your eyes, only to see a blur of darkness. Your headache and dizziness make it impossible to move.
After a while, you gradually regain your vision, then you notice a purple flower grown on the back of your hand.
Meanwhile, Sumire is standing in front of you in silence.
The Garden, the assassination, the FAC, the Mentor, the words Sumire said... A huge flood of information run through your brain, finally boiling down to one conclusion.
Sumire is here to kill you.

options: Remove the flower on your hand

choices.text: Remove the flower on your hand

steps.content: You try shouting to alert the guards, but you are too weak to make any sound that can be heard outside this room.
You try to remove that eerie little purple flower on the back of your hand, but a thousand pounds seem to be pressing down your arms. You simply can't move.
You realize you have probably been shot with some neurotoxin. It's only a matter of time before you die.
The intense headache stops you from focusing, and you can't even use the shackles.
That is your last hope dashed.

options: Are you here to kill me?

choices.text: Are you here to kill me?

steps.content: You hope Sumire will deny it straight away, but she doesn't answer.
After a long while, Sumire finally speaks. On her face is her usual smile, yet with an unfamiliar hint of resigned bitterness.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Remember... that letter?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It's an order from the Mentor.
They managed to sneak the letter into the FAC's files... The Garden is not to be underestimated indeed.
Your speech is slow and slightly slurred, but Sumire seems to be listening patiently.
If it was an assassination order, aren't you here a little too late?
What was the point of the letter if you received the order already? To risk exposing you?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The mission to assassinate you was posted a long time ago.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The letter was an ultimatum to me.
So you deliberately exposed yourself and got captured by the Bureau.
Was it all part of the Garden's plan?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: You must... be very disappointed.
No, just a little regretful.
I should've been more cautious.
A clear glint of sorrow flashes through Sumire's eyes.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It shouldn't have ended like this...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I was hoping things didn't have to end this way.
Sumire's voice overflows with sorrow. It's almost as if she is an ordinary woman who has come to your office to talk about her misfortunes in life.
But she is no ordinary woman. She has come all the way to the Bureau, evading all the security, just to kill you.
Why don't you just do it?
With a bitter smile, Sumire shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: No, you don't understand what I meant... I...
Sumire seems to be caught in a tangle of hesitation and distress. After a long while, she finally speaks again, in a whisper.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...When I used to create my ikebana works, I'd always give them a story.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Let me tell you a story this time.
A wave of intense headache hits you once more. Everything becomes a blur. All you can make out is Sumire's voice.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Once upon a time in Syndicate, there was a girl named Nana...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: One day, Nana's parents went missing, then the hooligans in the neighborhood started pestering her.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana couldn't fight back and almost died. That was when a lady showed up.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The lady gave Nana a knife and two options—either kill the hooligans, leave Syndicate, and join her organization to be her mentee; or just die like that.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana just wanted to survive.
Sumire pauses, which gives you time to figure out the meaning of the story. There is no doubt that "Nana" in this story is Sumire herself.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The training in the organization... was incredibly harsh. Some died, while those who survived were able to gain power to survive in a city like this.
Sinners...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Yes... Nana worked very hard and managed to survive the trials and even gained power—a power strong enough to defend herself even in a city like this.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana worked very hard and was very lucky, she survived the trials. The Mentor... the lady was very pleased with Nana's growth.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: She gave Nana a new name and taught her the art of ikebana, which gave her the ability to get a foothold in Eastside... she gave Nana everything Nana has today.
She's just controlling Nana.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana knew that, but she didn't care. She just wanted to repay her Mentor.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana had completed every mission the Mentor gave her, without the slightest hesitation, and without failure. Step by step, she became almost the best assassin in the organization.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Until she met the last assassination target... Nana failed that mission.
Why did she fail?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...The longer one has been as a Sinner, the easier it is to perceive the intangible.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It haunts everyone, along with the gift of the ability. It's like the Garden... It gives you the hope of new life along with the "gift" of pain.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But when Nana first approached the target, she found that those hallucinations haunting her for so long had disappeared, which caused her to miss the opportunity.
Then what happened next?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana observed the person for a long time. He wasn't stubborn like the FAC guys, neither was he blind as the Eastsiders who chased after her.
steps.female_content: Nana observed the person for a long time. She wasn't stubborn like the FAC guys, neither was she blind as the Eastsiders who chased after her.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: He would think about whether he was doing the right thing... The Sinners with him were never puppets who only carried out orders... They were all happy.
steps.female_content: She would think about whether she was doing the right thing... The Sinners with her were never puppets who only carried out orders... They were all happy.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana had never met anyone like that before. At first it was just curiosity, but then she became envious... Before Nana realized it, she could no longer bring herself to assassinate him.
steps.female_content: Nana had never met anyone like that before. At first it was just curiosity, but then she became envious... Before Nana realized it, she could no longer bring herself to assassin her.

steps.content: He was probably just doing what he should.
steps.female_content: She was probably just doing what she should.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: To do what you should do... It's never easy.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: In ikebana, the standard for the highest craftsmanship is... "like flowers in the wild." No matter how much flowers in vases resemble being in the wild, they are still rootless.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But this time, Nana felt that she had found the land she could truly fall back on.
Sumire takes a deep breath. The dizziness starts to fade, and her voice becomes clearer and clearer.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: When Nana returned, the Mentor didn't punish her for her failure but simply sent another assassin to cover her mistake.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But not only did Nana not appreciate her Mentor's mercy, but she also repeatedly sabotaged the assassinations and even injured her friend.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Later, Nana even exposed herself and went to that person.
Are you saying that Nana is protecting the assassination target?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...She just couldn't watch that person die.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana fended several attacks, but she became more and more worried...
Why?
Sumire gave you a sorrowful smile.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Because of...
...The Mentor?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...Yes, the Mentor.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Everyone in the organization learned to kill and the skills to make a living from the Mentor. No one can defeat her.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The Mentor has endless patience with her "creations." But she has zero tolerance for betrayal.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: And Nana... betrayed her.
Despair surfaces in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Nana hoped for the chance that the Mentor might not care about such a trivial matter, or that she still has sentiments for her mentees.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But that letter shattered all her hope. The Mentor would not let them go. If Nana didn't act, the Mentor would deal with it herself.
...I see.
Sumire shakes her head.
The chilling light slants through the window on her, but as if only shining into a darkest corner—only those eyes are glinting with faint shimmers.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: You won't understand.
Sumire looks out of the window at the sky.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I must leave now.
Leave?!
According to Sumire, she betrayed the Mentor. That letter has given her the last chance to prove her loyalty.
You're not killing me?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I will go to my Mentor and ask her to revoke the assassination order...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I will not let you die.
Will your Mentor let you off if you go back?
Sumire gives a smile again, gentle and friendly just as always, only with tears in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Meeting you was the luckiest thing that happened in my life.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I never deserved to be named after the flower, Sumire. I'm just a venomous insect that lurks in a dark corner and causes harm.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But You barged into the darkness and brought me a beam of... light. Now it's time to return to the darkness, for this beam of light.
Sumire turns around.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Farewell.
You force yourself back up on your feet, trying to use the shackles to stop her from leaving.
But an intense headache knocks you off balance, and you fall heavily onto the ground.
Sumire has already walked to the door, but turns back at the noise. She's standing in the dark and you can't see her expression on her face, but you notice her shoulders slightly shivering.
Finally, Sumire turns around and disappears into the dark.
You don't know how long it's been before you wake up again and everything around you gradually becomes clear.
Traces of fighting are all over the room—blood, a broken bookcase, an empty syringe, and a small metal can.
You struggle back up and switch on the security camera in the office.

steps.speaker: Female Voice
steps.content: Are you really going to betray the Mentor, Sumire?

steps.speaker: Female Voice
steps.content: For this man?!

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Okay.

steps.speaker: Female Voice
steps.content: He must die.
The woman raises the blade.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...I'm saving him.
In a split second, Sumire turns sideways and dodges a fatal stab. The blade in her hand sweeps across a lock of hair, and a flower of blood blooms at her opponent's right eye.
A grunt sounds. The attacker kneels on the floor, covering her eye. Sumire slowly steps forward to take her bag.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It's antidote... I knew there's still a chance to turn things around.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Go and tell the Mentor I'll go back to see her.
Sumire watches the woman leave, then turns toward you, and injects the antidote into your hand.
Then you wake up in the footage.
You lift your hand and find no purple flower but a tiny hole from injection.
Sumire never meant to kill you. You were wrong about her.
You hobble out of the Bureau following Sumire's trail.
You can still use your ability to sense her location using your connection with the Sinners. Your head still hurt, but it hardly stops you from moving now.
You can't let her just leave like this. You have to find her.
